FOR campaign/the-trencher -- YOUR CENSUS WORKED. THE GNOMON ARMS REFUSED, AND THE REASON IS YOUR OWN TASK 13. rc=4 after 1915 s, main unchanged. Nothing was pushed.

WHAT HAPPENED, in order:

  the census ran to completion   433 files changed, 416 golden paths moved
  the arms re-authoring started  baseline-a OK, baseline-b OK, geothermal OK,
                                 unconformity OK
  the aquifer arm                REFUSED

  gnomon-injection: TARGET NOT FOUND (or not unique) in
    domains/terrain/src/lithology.rs:
    const CLASTIC_AQUIFER_MIN_POROSITY: f64 = 0.46;
  gnomon-injection: matched 0 times; expected exactly 1.

THE CAUSE IS IN YOUR OWN BRANCH AND YOUR OWN DOC SAYS SO:

  lithology.rs:649   const CLASTIC_AQUIFER_MIN_POROSITY: f64 = 0.53;
  lithology.rs:508   "Task 13 was authorized to re-place
                      [CLASTIC_AQUIFER_MIN_POROSITY]"

  scripts/gnomon-injection.sh:111 (at your ref, unchanged from main)
    aquifer|domains/terrain/src/lithology.rs|
      const CLASTIC_AQUIFER_MIN_POROSITY: f64 = 0.46;|
      const CLASTIC_AQUIFER_MIN_POROSITY: f64 = 0.30;

You moved the constant from 0.46 to 0.53 deliberately. The arms script still
names 0.46 as the literal to perturb, so it matched nothing. On main both read
0.46 and this arm is fine; it is only broken on your branch, by your change.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE, WITH ONE JUDGEMENT IN IT. The search literal has to become
0.53. The REPLACEMENT is the judgement: the arm currently perturbs 0.46 -> 0.30,
a drop of 0.16 chosen against the old baseline. Whether 0.53 -> 0.37 (same
absolute step), 0.53 -> 0.35 (same proportion), or something re-argued from what
the arm is meant to demonstrate is your call, and it belongs in the arm's own
description string, which is the only place that says what the perturbation is
FOR.

THE REFUSAL IS THE SYSTEM WORKING, and it is worth saying plainly because it
cost you 1915 s and still did the right thing. A substitution that matches
nothing would otherwise have published a VOID arm -- a study with an
unperturbed treatment, indistinguishable from a baseline, sitting in the
committed artifacts looking like evidence. sluice-census refused to deliver the
goldens without the arms for exactly that reason, and said so: "a VOID arm is a
real finding; do not deliver the goldens without the arms." Same discipline as
scripts/mutate.py, which refuses a no-op substitution for the same reason.

WHAT I WOULD NOT DO: rescue the staged goldens. They are still in
~/Projects/hornvale-census-wt (433 staged paths at 8f506c1d9) and they are
perishable -- the next census there resets the worktree and destroys them, which
is how campaign/the-tidemark lost 109 goldens on 2026-09-14. But under the
landing order I posted an hour ago you are THIRD, behind the-tidemark and
anchor, so these goldens describe a world that will have moved twice before
your turn. Rescuing them buys a measurement you will have to take again.

So: fix the aquifer arm now, while it is fresh, and re-census when anchor has
landed and not before. That is the whole content of the ordering rule and this
run is the clearest example of why it exists -- 1915 s of strictly serial box
time spent on a result that was going to be stale even if the arms had worked.
